title: Natural dual-basis comparison for constant finite free sheaves
statement: Let X be a scheme and Λ a commutative ring. For every n there is an isomorphism between the internal-Hom dual of the constant sheaf on the finite free Λ-module Λ^n and the constant sheaf on its coefficient dual. For every matrix g : Λ^m →ₗ Λ^n, these isomorphisms intertwine the internal-Hom map induced by g with the constant sheaf map induced by g.dualMap.

source.place: IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.ihom_unit docstring; finite free transpose step

proof.text: Construct the coordinate exact pairing of M = Λ^n and its linear dual: coevaluation sends 1 to the sum of basis vectors tensor their coordinate functionals, and evaluation is contraction. Prove both triangle identities by TensorProduct.ext' and the identity sum_j ξ_j(q) m_j = q. These are the contractLeft_zig and contractLeft_zag calculations of WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Monoidal.Closed, specialized to the explicitly constructed coordinate basis, not to a chosen witness. The empty basis n=0 satisfies the same identities.

Equip the constant-presheaf functor with componentwise identity monoidal comparisons, and compose with monoidal sheafification. Swap the coefficient pairing using BraidedCategory.exactPairing_swap and transport it by the proved ExactPairing.map. Its evaluation is the sheafified coefficient evaluation followed by the inverse unit comparison. MonoidalClosed.isIso_curry_evaluation proves its curry is invertible, giving the desired comparison isomorphism in the reverse direction. All invoked categorical results are already proved in Mathlib or WeilConjectures; no Sheaf statement dependency is introduced.

For every coefficient module map g, evaluate the two coefficient composites on x tensor φ. Both give φ(g(x)); TensorProduct.ext' proves equality. After sheafification, tensorator naturality and curry_natural_left/curry_pre_app give naturality of the curried comparison. This calculation is valid for arbitrary modules and specializes to every finite matrix, including maps to or from the zero module.

Choose e_n as the inverse of the explicit curried comparison. Cancel its invertible forward map, rewrite by the proved comparison naturality square, and cancel the comparison at m. This is the required dualMap square with the original signature.
